channel.title: The Grant Desk - Fellowships, AI, Tech & Research, Europe, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Fellowships, AI, Tech & Research, Europe, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: IAS CEU: Global Invisible University Artist and Writer in Residence Fellowships 2027/28 (Budapest, EUR 2,000 a month) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Institute for Advanced Study, Central European University (IAS CEU)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: Net allowance of EUR 2,000 a month, plus accommodation at the Raoul Wallenberg Guesthouse and/or office space at IAS CEU as available. Travel and health insurance are not covered.

Two residential fellowships within the Global Invisible University programme: one Writer in Residence (poetry, prose, drama, screen and playwriting) and one Visual or New Media Artist in Residence (from painting and film to digital art, computer graphics and interactive art).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Humboldt Residency Programme 2027, "Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet" (funded six-week residency for researchers, creatives and practitioners) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Monthly allowance for the six-week residency (figure not published: researchers get standard Humboldt fellowship rates, creatives and practitioners a competitive honorarium), travel allowance to and from Germany, accommodation at Schloss Wiepersdorf and a Berlin aparthotel, and a budget for public formats. No family allowance. No application fee.

Each year the Humboldt Foundation brings twelve people from research, the arts and civil society together to work on one topic and find new ways of communicating it to audiences beyond academia. The 2027 topic is Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers (France) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Campus France, for the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: EUR 2,500 a month for 12 months, plus a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and health, civil liability and repatriation insurance. International travel is not covered.

Tenth call of Make Our Planet Great Again, a French government visiting fellowship for early career researchers to spend 12 months in a French laboratory.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Schloss Wiepersdorf Individual and Collaborative Fellowships 2028 (Brandenburg; EUR 1,200/month plus room and board) (closes 15 Apr 2027)
item.description:
Schloss Wiepersdorf (state of Brandenburg)
Deadline: 15 Apr 2027, 23:59 CEST
Award: EUR 1,200 per month stipend, a one-time EUR 480 material grant, room and board, and German visa costs where needed. No application fee.

Three-month residential fellowships at Schloss Wiepersdorf for artists, writers, composers and scholars from Germany and abroad. Fellows get room, board, a EUR 1,200 monthly stipend and a material grant; fine artists get a studio where space allows.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: KB Fellowship at NIAS 2027-2028 (National Library of the Netherlands collections incl. born-digital; artists and researchers) (closes 15 Mar 2027)
item.description:
NIAS-KNAW (Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study) with the KB, National Library of the Netherlands
Deadline: 15 Mar 2027, 12:00 CET
Award: Personal stipend (figure not published); scholars at Dutch institutions get a Dutch University Grant paid to their institution instead. Office, subsidised Amsterdam housing where eligible (otherwise local transport reimbursement). No application fee.

One fellowship a year for work with the KB's collections, facilities and expertise, including its large digitised and born-digital holdings.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Weizenbaum Institute: Affiliated Fellowship with a research group (Berlin; EUR 3,000 to 5,000/month, rolling)
item.description:
Weizenbaum Institute for the Networked Society
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Monthly allowance of EUR 3,000 (doctoral), EUR 4,000 (postdoc incl. assistant/associate professors) or EUR 5,000 (professors); EUR 2,500 / 3,500 if salary continues. Plus EUR 500/month child allowance and a travel lump sum of EUR 200 (Germany), 500 (Europe) or 1,200 (outside Europe). No application fee.

Short guest fellowships embedded in Weizenbaum Institute research groups working on platforms, digital society, AI and technology. ELIGIBILITY: researchers from doctoral candidates upward; artists are not mentioned.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Jane Street Graduate Research Fellowship 2027 (tuition plus USD 50,000 stipend) (closes 13 Nov)
item.description:
Jane Street
Deadline: 13 Nov 2026
Award: Full tuition and fees for the award year plus a USD 50,000 stipend (or local-currency equivalent; taxable). Finalists receive USD 5,000. No application fee.

Jane Street's Graduate Research Fellowship supports exceptional doctoral students in electrical engineering and computer science, mathematics, physics or statistics; research does not need to relate to trading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 (ZZF Potsdam, contemporary history)
item.description: Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam (ZZF) · deadline 30 Nov 2026 · Two fellowships of EUR 3,000 per month for two months (EUR 6,000 total each), plus office space, computer facilities, specialist library access and participation in ZZF's academic community. No application fee.
